approved: Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would make multiple changes to the rules for gaining and keeping Australian citizenship.
It would tighten character and residence requirements, expand cancellation and revocation powers, and allow personal information to be shared between citizenship and migration systems.

The maximum time the minister can postpone the citizenship pledge would be increased, and mandatory cancellation of approval would apply if the minister later finds the applicant would not pass identity, national security or criminal offence checks.
Extend good character requirements to all citizenship applicants including those under 18.
Allow the minister to cancel approval of citizenship if the applicant would no longer meet identity, national security or criminal offence rules before taking the pledge.
Give the minister discretion to revoke citizenship obtained by descent, conferral or intercountry adoption if it was gained by fraud or misrepresentation.
Increase the maximum period the minister can defer a person making the citizenship pledge.
Enable personal information collected under the Citizenship Act to be used or disclosed for Migration Act purposes.
Replace an automatic loss of citizenship by descent with a ministerial discretion to revoke it.
Australian citizenship applicants, current citizens, and the Department of Immigration and Border Protection.
Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 - Second Reading - Agree with bill's main idea

Introduced the Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, which would let the minister revoke citizenship for fraud without a prior conviction, extend the good character requirement to applicants under 18, extend the maximum delay before the pledge of commitment from 12 months to two years, and let the minister set aside Administrative Appeals Tribunal decisions after cases where it found applicants of good character despite convictions for offences including child sexual abuse and manslaughter.

Argued Labor would oppose the Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 on procedural grounds, saying members had seen the bill and its roughly 100 pages of explanatory material only since the previous Thursday and needed two more weeks to properly scrutinise it.

Supported the citizenship bill, highlighting new powers to revoke citizenship for fraud or misrepresentation without a prior conviction, extending the good character test to applicants under 18, and standardising a 12-month waiting period before resumption of citizenship.

Supported the citizenship bill, marking the 65th anniversary of Australian citizenship, and highlighted the extension of the minister's power to delay the pledge of commitment from 12 months to two years, while citing an estimated 1,200 deaths among people attempting dangerous journeys to Australia.

Argued that the Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 would strengthen citizenship integrity, identity and character requirements, allow citizenship revocation for fraud or misrepresentation without a prior conviction, and extend the minister's delay power from one year to two years.

Supported the Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014, said 48.3 per cent of people in the Barton electorate were born overseas, and outlined the bill's three themes of strengthening program integrity, emphasising connection to Australia, and improving ministerial decision-making including power to revoke citizenship obtained through fraud.

Summed up debate on the Australian Citizenship and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2014, defended giving the minister power to overturn Administrative Appeals Tribunal decisions that found applicants of good character despite convictions for child sexual offences, manslaughter or people smuggling, and said the bill extends from 12 months to two years the maximum time a pledge of commitment can be delayed during an investigation.
